subject: RE: Aptiv Dedicated renewal — sustained concurrency sizing
content:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@aptivsolutions.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aptivsolutions.com
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated renewal — sustained concurrency / sizing question

Hi Rishi,

We're starting our internal renewal planning for our Redwood Dedicated pool and need to validate sizing assumptions before we commit. Q4 2026 showed a clear increase in sustained concurrency during business hours (UTC-8), not just sporadic peaks. I've attached our utilization extract for Q4 (aptiv_q4_utilization_export.csv).

Quick background: we're currently on a 96-H100 equivalent tranche. Over the last three months our 95th percentile token-concurrency per minute rose from ~420 to ~610 live sessions. Latency and error rates stayed acceptable, but our warm-start and KV cache pressure do look like they contributed to the jump.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood model the minimal tranche add (and a mixed pool option with 40 H100 + 56 L40s) to keep 95p latency within our SLO under sustained load?
- What does a staged 90 -> 128 GPU ramp look like (both pricing and lead time for capacity)?

We'd like a sizing plan and a proposal by next Tuesday so Procurement can start the paperwork. Happy to jump on a quick call — Olivia.

--
Olivia Park
Head of Platform, Aptiv Solutions
olivia.park@aptivsolutions.com

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@aptivsolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated renewal — sustained concurrency / sizing question

Thanks, Olivia — good context and helpful extract. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Karthik (capacity planning) to lay out options. We should also review your KV cache hit rates and average prompt lengths; those drive the effective capacity more than raw GPU count.

Quick thoughts:
- Short-term: a +32 H100 tranche targeted at business hours (12-week commitment) should bring you back under the 95p latency SLO for sustained concurrency.
- Hybrid option: 40 H100 + 56 L40 provides cost flexibility; L40s handle warm-start and long-context workloads if we tune kernel selection and quantization profiles.
- Timing: Dedicated tranche provisioning typically 3–6 weeks for reserved capacity, 2–3 weeks if we can flex into our burst pool.

Marissa/Karthik — can you run a quick simulation against Olivia's CSV and produce: (1) a minimal add plan, (2) a hybrid mixed-pool proposal, (3) a staged ramp with pricing tiers and DocuSign-ready terms?

Rishi
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@aptivsolutions.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated renewal — sustained concurrency / sizing question

Olivia — thanks for the CSV, I pulled a few quick aggregates overnight. High-level summary:
- 7-day rolling average 95p concurrency (business hours): 585 sessions/min
- Median prompt length: 1.2k tokens; 95p prompt length: 3.9k tokens
- KV cache hit-rate during peak windows: 64% (opportunity to improve with prefix caching)

Given those numbers, my recommendation:
1) Short window safety bump: add 24 H100 as a targeted business-hour tranche. This reduces sustained 95p latency by ~18–22% in our sim.
2) Medium-term: transition to a hybrid 40 H100 + 56 L40 plan — optimizes cost while preserving tail latency when we serve long-context requests. We'll need a 4-week tuning window for quantization and kernel selection.
3) Staged ramp: Commit to 24 H100 now, then convert 16 of the next tranche to L40 later in Q1 if tuning metrics look good.

I've attached a working proposal draft (redwood_dedicated_proposal_v3.pdf) with pricing tiers and ramp schedules. Connor, can you add thermal/headroom assumptions and estimated lead times?

-Marissa
Head of Sales, Dedicated Products
marissa_cole@redwood.com

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@aptivsolutions.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity plan and simulation outputs

Attaching the simulation CSV and a short runbook (aptiv_procurement_matrix.xlsx). Key items from the sim:
- Baseline (96 H100): expected 95p latency under current sustained load = 1.15x SLO (mild breach)
- +24 H100 tranche: reduces tail pressure to 0.93x SLO during business hours (win)
- Hybrid 40H100+56L40: modeled cost savings ~18% vs homogeneous H100 plan; expected 95p latency within SLO after 4 weeks of tuning

Operational notes:
- KV cache warmup: recommend enabling prefix caching for your top 300 prompt templates — should improve hit rate by ~10–12% and reduce token load on GPUs during the first 60s of sessions.
- Batching policy: set an aggressive latency cap for business hours (max batch wait 8ms) and revert outside business hours to increase throughput.
- Fallback: maintain a small burst buffer of 8 H100s for thermal or unexpected spikes.

I'll attach the simulation output for your procurement team. Lead time estimate: 3 weeks for tranche allocation if we use existing pool; 5–6 weeks if we need dedicated procurement.

-Karthik
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Team — this is excellent, thanks. A few clarifying items from Procurement:
- We prefer a staged commitment with a 90-day evaluation clause before the second tranche is billed. Is that feasible?
- What's the SLA delta if we mix L40s in the pool — specifically, do we get the same tail-latency SLO credits or is there an explicit penalty?

If you can provide a single-page commercial summary and a DocuSign-ready amendment, we'll route it through Procurement this week.

Olivia

Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:37:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Aptiv Dedicated renewal — sustained concurrency sizing

Olivia — confirmed, we can do a staged commitment with a 90-day evaluation clause for the second tranche. Commercial summary and DocuSign amendment attached via HubSpot link (see related_links).

SLA + hybrid pools: we treat the pool as a single logical capacity for SLO calculation; if the hybrid pool is provisioned and tuned per our runbook (we'll accept a short tuning SLA), you will receive the same 95p tail-latency coverage. Any temporary deviation during the 4-week tuning window will be captured in the evaluation clause rather than SLA credits.

Action items:
- Marissa: finalize the one-page commercial summary and attach to DocuSign (due EOD Wed)
- Karthik: confirm thermal/headroom numbers and final lead times in the procurement matrix (update by Wed morning)
- Olivia: confirm Proc team's preferred billing contact and send PO template if available

I'll update the HubSpot deal and push the DocuSign envelope once Marissa uploads the summary. Thanks all — Rishi
